extracted.intended_audience: Authors and researchers reporting healthcare quality improvement (QI) and patient-safety intervention studies for publication
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and reporting healthcare improvement interventions (design, context, measures, analysis, ethics, and results) so that others can evaluate, reproduce, and generalise findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific aims
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific aim of a project describes why it was conducted, and the goal of the report. It is essential to state the aims of improvement work clearly, completely and precisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific aims should align with the nature and significance of the problem, the gap in quality, safety and value identified in the introduction, and reflect the rationale for the intervention(s). When appropriate, the specific aims section should state that both process and outcomes will be assessed; focusing only on outcomes ignores whether clinicians adopted the desired practice or adopted it effectively. Use examples (eg, goal to improve/reduce postoperative respiratory failure) to make the aim precise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe contextual factors important at the outset of the improvement initiative to assist readers in understanding where the initiative occurred and whether findings generalise to other settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specifics for single-centre studies (location, patient population, size, staffing, practice type, teaching status, system affiliation, relevant processes) and aggregate descriptions for multicentre studies. Report how sites/practices were selected (eg, to represent diversity). Explain contextual choices that may limit generalisability (eg, selecting practices with prior QI experience or available incentives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of published frameworks for context
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider using published frameworks to identify relevant contextual factors to be examined (eg, MUSIQ, CFIR, PARiHS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a framework when appropriate to determine which contextual elements to address; select the framework based on the focus of the work (MUSIQ for microsystem/organisational QI; CFIR and PARiHS for broader implementation). Framework use is optional but helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective measurement of contextual factors
rubrics_metrics.description: If elements of context are hypothesised to be important, plans should be made a priori to measure these contextual factors prospectively during study design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If planning prospective measurement, specify measurement methods in the methods section, include data about interactions between context and interventions in results, and explore implications in discussion. If context was not addressed prospectively, authors are encouraged to explore context's impact in the discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention description sufficient for reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the intervention(s) in sufficient detail that others could reproduce it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe each component of multimodal interventions, provide brief descriptions with references to fuller descriptions (eg, TIDieR guidelines), supply online supplementary appendices summarising key elements, and note situations where the intervention differed across sites. Report every change that could have contributed to outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify implementation details and integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the intervention was integrated into routine processes (eg, oral and written handoffs expected for every patient; tools built into electronic medical records).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report implementation logs, how tools were embedded (EMR vs word-processing), expectations for use (eg, oral + written handoff for every patient), and materials used to promote adoption (logos, posters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe the team and personnel involved
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the characteristics of the team that conducted the intervention and the personnel to whom the intervention was applied (type and level of training, degree of experience, administrative/academic position).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report influence of people involved; include details such as who led workshops, who performed audits, and characteristics of staff being studied. This helps readers judge potential influence of personnel on outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report variation and fidelity of implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Report variation in application of intervention components across units, sites, or clinicians and assess fidelity of implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note when elements differed across sites (eg, two sites used word-processing instead of EMR), maintain implementation logs, and include evaluation of fidelity (observations, adherence checks) as part of study of the intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design for assessing impact
rubrics_metrics.description: State and justify the approach chosen for assessing the impact of the intervention(s) (eg, stepped wedge, comparison control group, time-series, quasi-experimental designs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a design aligned with aims and rationale; describe how the design helps answer whether the intervention caused observed changes, and plan analyses accordingly (eg, multiple time points before/after, use of control sites).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to establish causality/internal validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the approach used to establish whether observed outcomes were due to the intervention(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparison groups, time-series analysis, quasi-experimental designs, statistical tests, and account for confounders (eg, system-wide policy changes). Describe analyses designed to distinguish intervention effects from other causes and any sensitivity checks (eg, assess unintended impacts such as mortality or complication rates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of evaluative techniques and who performed them
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the aims and methods for studying the intervention and indicate whether evaluative techniques were performed by the authors or an outside team and their relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State timing of evaluation activities relative to the intervention, whether PDSA cycles were used, and whether stakeholder feedback (patients, families, staff) was collected via surveys, interviews, focus groups, or observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures — selection, rationale, operational definitions, validity/reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Report measures chosen for studying processes and outcomes, including rationale for choosing them, their operational definitions, and their validity and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine multiple perspectives (clinical, functional, experiential, cost). Provide references/documentation for validated instruments, explain selection of subsets of survey items, and describe how measures capture intended constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing assessment of contextual elements (including cost/efficiency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the approach to the ongoing assessment of contextual elements that contributed to the success, failure, efficiency, and cost of the improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prospective measurement or include plans to examine context–intervention interactions. Report data and analyses that examine how contextual factors moderated outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for assessing completeness and accuracy of data
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods employed for assessing completeness and accuracy of data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report how data completeness and accuracy were checked (eg, double data entry, audits, validation against external sources) so readers can appraise trustworthiness of inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis methods — qualitative and quantitative aligned to aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe qualitative and quantitative methods used to draw inferences from the data and ensure analytical strategy aligns with the rationale, project aims and data constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain choice of methods (eg, SPC, Pareto charts, χ2 tests, time-series, regression, grounded theory), provide brief rationale for each, and cite methods to allow readers to find further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for understanding variation and time effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide methods for understanding variation within the data, including the effects of time as a variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use control charts, run charts, statistical process control with rules for special vs common cause variation, line graphs, small multiples, rational subgrouping, and regression to test slopes. Explain limitations (eg, insufficient baseline points) and how chosen methods address them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative analysis rigor and triangulation
rubrics_metrics.description: When using qualitative methods, document systematic techniques to ensure validity (eg, coding frameworks, double coding, triangulation, noting deviant cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe interview guides, audiotaping and transcription, independent double coding, constant comparative approach, and triangulation of investigator memos to support analytic decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report unintended consequences and multiple outcome dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and report both intended and unintended (desired or undesired) changes in outcomes, and combine multiple outcome dimensions (clinical, functional, experiential, cost).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include analyses to detect adverse impacts (eg, operative mortality) and use triangulation of different data sources to strengthen inferences about outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical review and competing interests disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly describe how potential ethical concerns were reviewed and addressed, including whether independent ethics review occurred, and report potential conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the ethics approvals or local review mechanisms used (which may vary by country/institution), indicate where the work was reviewed (eg, regional research ethics committee or quality management office), and provide transparent competing interests statements (including employment, royalties, advisory roles, shareholders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Results — evolution, timeline and modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the initial steps of the intervention(s) and their evolution over time, including modifications made to the intervention during the project (eg, timeline diagram, flow chart or table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timelines/flowcharts/tables showing phases, document tests of change and analyses, and describe how the intervention evolved across phases and sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results — detail process measures and outcomes (sustainability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report details of the process measures and outcome results, including metrics, statistical/process-control evidence, and evidence of sustainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present numeric results (eg, percent receiving antibiotics within 60 minutes increased from X to Y), control charts demonstrating reliability and sustainment over months/years, and list key improvement areas and specific interventions implemented. Use figures (control charts, small multiples) to demonstrate changes and variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and representativeness of sites/participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how sites/participants were recruited/selected and whether they were chosen to represent diversity in practice types, settings, and patient populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report recruitment methods (eg, through networks), whether incentives or prior experience influenced selection, and implications for generalisability.
